source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / Directorate General of Agriculture, "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះសណ្តែកសៀង" [Soybean cultivation techniques], official extension manual, 2018
text:
Land selection: soybean is described as adaptable to a wide range of land types except heavy-clay, poorly-drained fields, since the crop is intolerant of standing water. Organic-matter-rich soil is preferred since it favors root-nodule formation. Key soil nutrients named as needed are N, P, K, Ca, Mg, Fe, and S, and the manual notes soybean tolerates a fairly wide soil-fertility range compared to some crops, but performs best where rainfall/soil moisture is 10–15 mm every few days is available consistently through establishment.

Land preparation is done either with animal-drawn or tractor-drawn implements; the manual recommends ploughing at least 5–6 days before planting to let the soil settle and any incorporated organic matter begin breaking down, illustrated with photos of both cattle-drawn ploughing and tractor ploughing/discing.
